title: Grilled BBQ chicken thighs
summary: Bone-in thighs with a smoky paprika rub, cooked over indirect heat, then brushed with a sugar-free tomato glaze in the last minutes.

ingredients.note: 8 bone-in, skin-on thighs, about 2 kg (4½ lb); about 1.3 kg is meat and skin

steps: Pat the thighs dry. Mix the rub spices, toss the thighs with the oil, then with the rub. Rest 20 minutes, or refrigerate up to a day.
Whisk the glaze ingredients in a small pan and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Set up the grill for two zones: coals or burners on one side only, aiming for about 190 °C (375 °F) under the lid. Lay the thighs skin side up on the cool side.
Cover and cook 30–35 minutes, until a thermometer next to the bone reads 74 °C (165 °F); thighs are juicier taken to 80–85 °C (175–185 °F).
Move the thighs skin side down to the hot side for 2–3 minutes to crisp. Turn, brush with glaze and cook 1–2 minutes more; the glaze contains allulose and scorches fast.
Oven alternative: bake on a rack over a lined tray at 200 °C (400 °F) for 35–40 minutes, brush with glaze and grill under the broiler for 2 minutes.
tips: Worcestershire sauce contains anchovy; tamari is a fish-free swap.
Any of the sugar-free barbecue sauces in the sauces chapter can replace this glaze.

origin.history: Grilling chicken over coals and brushing it with sauce became a backyard ritual in post-war suburban America, helped along by cheap charcoal briquettes and the domed kettle grill, which was designed near Chicago in the early 1950s. This is a home cook's dish rather than one with a single birthplace; the map pin marks that grill's home.
